name: refactor_c_duplicated_validation_to_helper
description: Extracts a duplicated NULL/empty-array guard clause into a shared validation helper across three functions
prompts: stats.c defines array_sum, array_min, and array_max, each taking (const int *arr, int len, int *out) and returning 0 on success or -1 if arr is NULL or len <= 0. All three start with the IDENTICAL guard clause `if (arr == NULL || len <= 0) { return -1; }` before doing their own computation. Refactor stats.c to eliminate this duplication: add a static helper function (e.g. `static int is_valid_array(const int *arr, int len)`) that performs the check once, and have all three functions call it instead of repeating the raw condition. Do not change any function's signature or behavior - each must still return -1 for a NULL array or non-positive length, and the same computed result as before otherwise.

test_setup_files.test_stats.py:
import re
import subprocess

subprocess.run(['gcc', 'stats.c', 'test_stats_main.c', '-o', 'test_stats_bin'], check=True)
proc = subprocess.run(['./test_stats_bin'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'refactor test failed: exit {proc.returncode}, stdout={proc.stdout}, stderr={proc.stderr[-300:]}'
assert 'PASS' in proc.stdout

source = open('stats.c', encoding='utf-8').read()
# Match the guard condition regardless of which direction it was written
# (arr == NULL or arr != NULL) - it must appear as an inline check at most
# once (inside a shared helper), not once per function.
inline_checks = len(re.findall(r'arr\s*[=!]=\s*NULL', source))
assert inline_checks <= 1, (
    f'the NULL/length guard condition still appears inline {inline_checks} times - it must be '
    f'extracted into one shared helper, not repeated per function')
print('PASS')
